newsitem.title: INDIA: India says plans major steps on infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: India says plans major steps on infrastructure.

text.p: India said on Wednesday it would soon unveil a series of steps to improve its infrastructure facilities, a shortage of which is seen choking high economic growth.
"You should be hearing on the government's plans for infrastructure," Planning Minister Yogendra Alagh told a business seminar in the Indian capital.
He said the government would discuss infrastructure issues at length in its document for the Ninth Five Year Plan which is scheduled to start with the next financial year, 1997/98 (April-March).
"We would be coming up with very detailed policy guidelines in the next few months," Alagh said, specifying power and water supply as key facilities that needed improvement.
"The approach paper for the Ninth Plan will have considerable detail on power, roads and ports," the minister, who is also one of India's leading economists, told the seminar.
"That kind of reforms will push us in the right direction," Alagh said.
India sets its public spending priorities for five-year terms through its Planning Commission, which advises the government on policy measures and investment to meet growth targets.
India is using its five-year plans, which were once a socialist plannning instrument, to strengthen the foundation of free market reforms which started five years ago.
